title: From Java to C
objectives: Read input with scanf (each variable with its &) and print with printf, using widths and precision such as %7.2f.
Choose between char, int, unsigned and double, and predict integer division, char arithmetic and unsigned wrap-around.
Write if, loops and switch the C way, with break and deliberate fall-through.

readings.title: Lecture 1: C
readings.lookFor: From "Hello, World" to "Types", "Format Codes" and "Loops and meow.c". CS50 uses its own library: get_int and string come from cs50.h, which you don't have here. Read input with scanf instead, as in the example above.

readings.title: Input and output
readings.lookFor: Optional: the printf format specifiers and scanf with &. "Unsigned integers" and "The problem with overflow", earlier in the same handbook, explain the wrap-around.

pt-br.title: Do Java para o C
objectives: Ler a entrada com scanf (cada variável com seu &) e imprimir com printf, usando largura e precisão como %7.2f.
Escolher entre char, int, unsigned e double, e prever a divisão inteira, a aritmética com char e a volta dos unsigned.
Escrever if, laços e switch do jeito do C, com break e com queda proposital (fall-through).

readings.lookFor: De "Hello, World" até "Types", "Format Codes" e "Loops and meow.c". O CS50 usa uma biblioteca própria: get_int e string vêm de cs50.h, que você não tem aqui. Leia a entrada com scanf, como no exemplo acima.
Opcional: os especificadores de formato do printf e o scanf com &. "Unsigned integers" e "The problem with overflow", antes no mesmo livro, explicam a volta dos unsigned.
